<div class="domain-banner-text">
<div class="domain-heading">Disease Attributes</div>
<p class="domain-description">Disease Attributes contains diagnostic, staging, anatomic, histologic, biologic, risk, extent-of-disease, and disease-site concepts used to characterize the subject's cancer or cancer-related condition.</p>

<div class="domain-banner domain-intervention">
<div class="domain-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-hospital-icon lucide-hospital"><path d="M12 7v4"/><path d="M14 21v-3a2 2 0 0 0-4 0v3"/><path d="M14 9h-4"/><path d="M18 11h2a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v6a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H4a2 2 0 0 1-2-2v-9a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h2"/><path d="M18 21V5a2 2 0 0 0-2-2H8a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v16"/></svg></div>
<div class="domain-banner-text">
<div class="domain-heading">Intervention</div>
<p class="domain-description">Intervention contains treatment and procedure records, including surgery, medications, radiation therapy, transplantation, transfusion, cellular therapy, locoregional therapy, fertility preservation procedures, and protocol treatment modifications.</p>
</div>

<div class="domain-banner-text">
<div class="domain-heading">Monitoring</div>
<p class="domain-description">Monitoring contains response, residual disease, toxicity, late effects, subsequent neoplasms, reproductive outcomes, patient-reported outcomes, and other follow-up concepts used to evaluate disease course and treatment impact over time.</p>

The elevated activity of this agent in normal tissues results from both the relative abundance of alkaline phosphatase in normal tissues and the greater vascularity of normal tissues compared to tumor tissues."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>The trihydrate form of a phosphorylated aminosulfhydryl compound. After dephosphorylation of amifostine by alkaline phosphatase to an active free sulfhydryl (thiol) metabolite, the thiol metabolite binds to and detoxifies cytotoxic platinum-containing metabolites of cisplatin and scavenges free radicals induced by cisplatin and ionizing radiation. The elevated activity of this agent in normal tissues results from both the relative abundance of alkaline phosphatase in normal tissues and the greater vascularity of normal tissues compared to tumor tissues.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Amsacrine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Amsacrine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C240" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Amsacrine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C240"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C240</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An aminoacridine derivative with potential antineoplastic activity. Although its mechanism of action is incompletely defined, amsacrine may intercalate into DNA and inhibit topoisomerase II, resulting in DNA double-strand breaks, arrest of the S/G2 phase of the cell cycle, and cell death. This agent's cytotoxicity is maximal during the S phase of the cell cycle when topoisomerase levels are greatest. In addition, amsacrine may induce transcription of tumor promoter p53 protein and block p53 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, resulting in p53-dependent tumor cell apoptosis."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An aminoacridine derivative with potential antineoplastic activity. Although its mechanism of action is incompletely defined, amsacrine may intercalate into DNA and inhibit topoisomerase II, resulting in DNA double-strand breaks, arrest of the S/G2 phase of the cell cycle, and cell death. This agent's cytotoxicity is maximal during the S phase of the cell cycle when topoisomerase levels are greatest. In addition, amsacrine may induce transcription of tumor promoter p53 protein and block p53 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, resulting in p53-dependent tumor cell apoptosis.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Arsenic Trioxide"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Arsenic Trioxide" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1005" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Arsenic Trioxide</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1005"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1005</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug used to treat acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) that has not gotten better or that has come back after treatment with other anticancer drugs. It is also being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A drug used to treat acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) that has not gotten better or that has come back after treatment with other anticancer drugs. It is also being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Bendamustine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Bendamustine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C73261" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Bendamustine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C73261"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C73261</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A bifunctional mechlorethamine derivative with alkylating and antimetabolite activities. Although the exact mechanism of action of bendamustine is unknown, this agent appears to alkylate and crosslink macromolecules, resulting in DNA, RNA and protein synthesis inhibition, and eventually the induction of apoptosis."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A bifunctional mechlorethamine derivative with alkylating and antimetabolite activities. Although the exact mechanism of action of bendamustine is unknown, this agent appears to alkylate and crosslink macromolecules, resulting in DNA, RNA and protein synthesis inhibition, and eventually the induction of apoptosis.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Bleomycin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Bleomycin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C313" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Bleomycin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C313"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C313</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A mixture of glycopeptide antineoplastic antibiotics isolated from the bacterium Streptomyces verticillus. Bleomycin forms complexes with iron that reduce molecular oxygen to superoxide and hydroxyl radicals which cause single- and double-stranded breaks in DNA; these reactive oxygen species also induce lipid peroxidation, carbohydrate oxidation, and alterations in prostaglandin synthesis and degradation."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A mixture of glycopeptide antineoplastic antibiotics isolated from the bacterium Streptomyces verticillus. Bleomycin forms complexes with iron that reduce molecular oxygen to superoxide and hydroxyl radicals which cause single- and double-stranded breaks in DNA; these reactive oxygen species also induce lipid peroxidation, carbohydrate oxidation, and alterations in prostaglandin synthesis and degradation.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Bortezomib"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Bortezomib" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1851" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Bortezomib</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1851"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1851</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A dipeptide boronic acid analogue with antineoplastic activity. Bortezomib reversibly inhibits the 26S proteasome, a large protease complex that degrades ubiquinated proteins. By blocking the targeted proteolysis normally performed by the proteasome, bortezomib disrupts various cell signaling pathways, leading to cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, and inhibition of angiogenesis. Specifically, the agent inhibits nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB, a protein that is constitutively activated in some cancers, thereby interfering with NF-kappaB-mediated cell survival, tumor growth, and angiogenesis. In vivo, bortezomib delays tumor growth and enhances the cytotoxic effects of radiation and chemotherapy."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A dipeptide boronic acid analogue with antineoplastic activity. Bortezomib reversibly inhibits the 26S proteasome, a large protease complex that degrades ubiquinated proteins. By blocking the targeted proteolysis normally performed by the proteasome, bortezomib disrupts various cell signaling pathways, leading to cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, and inhibition of angiogenesis. Specifically, the agent inhibits nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB, a protein that is constitutively activated in some cancers, thereby interfering with NF-kappaB-mediated cell survival, tumor growth, and angiogenesis. In vivo, bortezomib delays tumor growth and enhances the cytotoxic effects of radiation and chemotherapy.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Brentuximab Vedotin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Brentuximab Vedotin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C66944" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Brentuximab Vedotin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C66944"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C66944</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) directed against the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) receptor CD30 with potential antineoplastic activity. Brentuximab vedotin is generated by conjugating the chimeric anti-CD30 monoclonal antibody SGN-30 to the cytotoxic agent monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via a valine-citrulline peptide linker. Upon administration and internalization by CD30-positive tumor cells, brentuximab vedotin undergoes enzymatic cleavage, releasing MMAE into the cytosol; MMAE binds to tubulin and inhibits tubulin polymerization, which may result in G2/M phase arrest and tumor cell apoptosis. Transiently activated during lymphocyte activation, CD30 (tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily, member 8;TNFRSF8) may be constitutively expressed in hematologic malignancies including Hodgkin lymphoma and some T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas. The linkage system in brentuximab vedotin is highly stable in plasma, resulting in cytotoxic specificity for CD30-positive cells."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) directed against the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) receptor CD30 with potential antineoplastic activity. Brentuximab vedotin is generated by conjugating the chimeric anti-CD30 monoclonal antibody SGN-30 to the cytotoxic agent monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via a valine-citrulline peptide linker. Upon administration and internalization by CD30-positive tumor cells, brentuximab vedotin undergoes enzymatic cleavage, releasing MMAE into the cytosol; MMAE binds to tubulin and inhibits tubulin polymerization, which may result in G2/M phase arrest and tumor cell apoptosis. Transiently activated during lymphocyte activation, CD30 (tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily, member 8;TNFRSF8) may be constitutively expressed in hematologic malignancies including Hodgkin lymphoma and some T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas. The linkage system in brentuximab vedotin is highly stable in plasma, resulting in cytotoxic specificity for CD30-positive cells.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Busulfan"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Busulfan" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C321" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Busulfan</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C321"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C321</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A synthetic derivative of dimethane-sulfonate with antineoplastic and cytotoxic properties.  Although its mechanism of action is not fully understood, busulfan appears to act through the alkylation of DNA.  Following systemic absorption of busulfan, carbonium ions are formed, resulting in DNA alkylation and DNA breaks and inhibition of DNA replication and RNA transcription. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A synthetic derivative of dimethane-sulfonate with antineoplastic and cytotoxic properties.  Although its mechanism of action is not fully understood, busulfan appears to act through the alkylation of DNA.  Following systemic absorption of busulfan, carbonium ions are formed, resulting in DNA alkylation and DNA breaks and inhibition of DNA replication and RNA transcription. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Carboplatin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Carboplatin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1282" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Carboplatin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1282"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1282</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug that is used to treat advanced ovarian cancer that has never been treated or symptoms of ovarian cancer that has come back after treatment with other anticancer drugs. It is also used with other drugs to treat advanced, metastatic, or recurrent non-small cell lung cancer and is being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. Paraplatin is a form of the anticancer drug cisplatin and causes fewer side effects in patients. It attaches to DNA in cells and may kill cancer cells. It is a type of platinum compound."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A drug that is used to treat advanced ovarian cancer that has never been treated or symptoms of ovarian cancer that has come back after treatment with other anticancer drugs. It is also used with other drugs to treat advanced, metastatic, or recurrent non-small cell lung cancer and is being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. Paraplatin is a form of the anticancer drug cisplatin and causes fewer side effects in patients. It attaches to DNA in cells and may kill cancer cells. It is a type of platinum compound.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Carmustine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Carmustine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C349" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Carmustine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C349"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C349</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An anticancer drug that belongs to the family of drugs called alkylating agents."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An anticancer drug that belongs to the family of drugs called alkylating agents.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Cisplatin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Cisplatin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C376" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Cisplatin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C376"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C376</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug used to treat many types of cancer. Cisplatin contains the metal platinum. It kills cancer cells by damaging their DNA and stopping them from dividing. Cisplatin is a type of alkylating agent."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A drug used to treat many types of cancer. Cisplatin contains the metal platinum. It kills cancer cells by damaging their DNA and stopping them from dividing. Cisplatin is a type of alkylating agent.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Cladribine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Cladribine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1336" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Cladribine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1336"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1336</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A purine nucleoside antimetabolite analogue. Cladribine triphosphate, a phosphorylated metabolite of cladribine, incorporates into DNA, resulting in single-strand breaks in DNA, depletion of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and adenosine triphosphate (ATP), and apoptosis.  Because this agent is resistant to adenosine deaminase, an enzyme that inactivates some antineoplastic agents, it is selectively toxic to lymphocytes and monocytes which exhibit little deoxynucleotide deaminase activity. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A purine nucleoside antimetabolite analogue. Cladribine triphosphate, a phosphorylated metabolite of cladribine, incorporates into DNA, resulting in single-strand breaks in DNA, depletion of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and adenosine triphosphate (ATP), and apoptosis.  Because this agent is resistant to adenosine deaminase, an enzyme that inactivates some antineoplastic agents, it is selectively toxic to lymphocytes and monocytes which exhibit little deoxynucleotide deaminase activity. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Daunorubicin (Liposomal)"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Daunorubicin (Liposomal)" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C2213" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Daunorubicin (Liposomal)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C2213"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C2213</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A liposome-encapsulated form of the citrate salt of the anthracycline antineoplastic antibiotic daunorubicin. Daunorubicin intercalates into DNA and interacts with topoisomerase II, thereby inhibiting DNA replication and repair and RNA and protein synthesis. Liposomal delivery of doxorubicin citrate improves drug penetration into tumors and decreases drug clearance, thereby increasing the duration of therapeutic drug effects."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A liposome-encapsulated form of the citrate salt of the anthracycline antineoplastic antibiotic daunorubicin. Daunorubicin intercalates into DNA and interacts with topoisomerase II, thereby inhibiting DNA replication and repair and RNA and protein synthesis. Liposomal delivery of doxorubicin citrate improves drug penetration into tumors and decreases drug clearance, thereby increasing the duration of therapeutic drug effects.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Daunorubicin and Cytarabine (Liposomal)"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Daunorubicin and Cytarabine (Liposomal)" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C67504" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Daunorubicin and Cytarabine (Liposomal)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C67504"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C67504</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A liposomal formulation containing a fixed combination of the antineoplastic agents cytarabine and daunorubicin in a 5:1 molar ratio. Liposome-encapsulated daunorubicin-cytarabine has been designed to provide optimal delivery of a specific ratio of cytarabine to daunorubicin, one that has been shown to be synergistic in vitro. The antimetabolite cytarabine competes with cytidine for incorporation into DNA, inhibiting DNA synthesis. This agent also inhibits DNA polymerase, resulting in a decrease in DNA replication and repair. Daunorubicin, an intercalator and a topoisomerase II inhibitor, prevents DNA replication and inhibits protein synthesis. This agent also generates oxygen free radicals, resulting in the cytotoxic lipid peroxidation of cell membrane lipids."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A liposomal formulation containing a fixed combination of the antineoplastic agents cytarabine and daunorubicin in a 5:1 molar ratio. Liposome-encapsulated daunorubicin-cytarabine has been designed to provide optimal delivery of a specific ratio of cytarabine to daunorubicin, one that has been shown to be synergistic in vitro. The antimetabolite cytarabine competes with cytidine for incorporation into DNA, inhibiting DNA synthesis. This agent also inhibits DNA polymerase, resulting in a decrease in DNA replication and repair. Daunorubicin, an intercalator and a topoisomerase II inhibitor, prevents DNA replication and inhibits protein synthesis. This agent also generates oxygen free radicals, resulting in the cytotoxic lipid peroxidation of cell membrane lipids.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Dexamethasone"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Dexamethasone" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C422" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Dexamethasone</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C422"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C422</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A synthetic adrenal corticosteroid with potent anti-inflammatory properties. In addition to binding to specific nuclear steroid receptors, dexamethasone also interferes with NF-kB activation and apoptotic pathways. This agent lacks the salt-retaining properties of other related adrenal hormones. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A synthetic adrenal corticosteroid with potent anti-inflammatory properties. In addition to binding to specific nuclear steroid receptors, dexamethasone also interferes with NF-kB activation and apoptotic pathways. This agent lacks the salt-retaining properties of other related adrenal hormones. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Doxorubicin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Doxorubicin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C456" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Doxorubicin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C456"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C456</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug that is used to treat many types of cancer and is being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. <tr data-subsets="base aml hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Fludarabine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Fludarabine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1094" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Fludarabine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1094"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1094</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A fluorinated nucleotide antimetabolite analog of the antiviral agent vidarabine (ara-A) with antineoplastic activity. Administered parenterally as a phosphate salt, fludarabine phosphate is rapidly dephosphorylated to 2-fluoro-ara-A and then phosphorylated intracellularly by deoxycytidine kinase to the active triphosphate, 2-fluoro-ara-ATP. This metabolite may inhibit DNA polymerase alpha, ribonucleotide reductase and DNA primase, thereby interrupting DNA synthesis and inhibiting tumor cell growth.  (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A fluorinated nucleotide antimetabolite analog of the antiviral agent vidarabine (ara-A) with antineoplastic activity. Administered parenterally as a phosphate salt, fludarabine phosphate is rapidly dephosphorylated to 2-fluoro-ara-A and then phosphorylated intracellularly by deoxycytidine kinase to the active triphosphate, 2-fluoro-ara-ATP. This metabolite may inhibit DNA polymerase alpha, ribonucleotide reductase and DNA primase, thereby interrupting DNA synthesis and inhibiting tumor cell growth.  (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Gemcitabine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Gemcitabine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C66876" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Gemcitabine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C66876"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C66876</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A broad-spectrum antimetabolite and deoxycytidine analogue with antineoplastic activity. Upon administration, gemcitabine is converted into the active metabolites difluorodeoxycytidine diphosphate (dFdCDP) and difluorodeoxycytidine triphosphate (dFdCTP) by deoxycytidine kinase. dFdCTP competes with deoxycytidine triphosphate (dCTP) and is incorporated into DNA.  This locks DNA polymerase thereby resulting in &quot;masked termination&quot; during DNA replication. On the other hand, dFdCDP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, thereby decreasing the deoxynucleotide pool available for DNA synthesis. The reduction in the intracellular concentration of dCTP potentiates the incorporation of dFdCTP into DNA."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A broad-spectrum antimetabolite and deoxycytidine analogue with antineoplastic activity. Upon administration, gemcitabine is converted into the active metabolites difluorodeoxycytidine diphosphate (dFdCDP) and difluorodeoxycytidine triphosphate (dFdCTP) by deoxycytidine kinase. dFdCTP competes with deoxycytidine triphosphate (dCTP) and is incorporated into DNA.  This locks DNA polymerase thereby resulting in "masked termination" during DNA replication. On the other hand, dFdCDP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, thereby decreasing the deoxynucleotide pool available for DNA synthesis. The reduction in the intracellular concentration of dCTP potentiates the incorporation of dFdCTP into DNA.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Gemtuzumab Ozogamicin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Gemtuzumab Ozogamicin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1806" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Gemtuzumab Ozogamicin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1806"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1806</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A monoclonal antibody combined with a toxic substance that is used to treat certain types of acute myeloid leukemia in older patients and is being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. Monoclonal antibodies are made in the laboratory and can locate and bind to substances in the body, including cancer cells. Mylotarg is a type of antibody-drug conjugate."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A monoclonal antibody combined with a toxic substance that is used to treat certain types of acute myeloid leukemia in older patients and is being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. Monoclonal antibodies are made in the laboratory and can locate and bind to substances in the body, including cancer cells. Mylotarg is a type of antibody-drug conjugate.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Gilteritinib"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Gilteritinib" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C116722" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Gilteritinib</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C116722"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C116722</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An orally bioavailable inhibitor of the receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3; STK1; FLK2), AXL (UFO; JTK11), anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK; CD246), and leukocyte receptor tyrosine kinase (LTK), with potential antineoplastic activity. Upon administration, gilteritinib binds to and inhibits both the wild-type and mutated forms of FLT3, AXL, ALK and LTK. This may result in an inhibition of FLT3-, AXL-, ALK-, and LTK-mediated signal transduction pathways and reduced proliferation in cancer cells that overexpress these RTKs. FLT3, AXL, ALK, and LTK, which are overexpressed or mutated in a variety of cancer cell types, play key roles in tumor cell growth and survival."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An orally bioavailable inhibitor of the receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3; STK1; FLK2), AXL (UFO; JTK11), anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK; CD246), and leukocyte receptor tyrosine kinase (LTK), with potential antineoplastic activity. Upon administration, gilteritinib binds to and inhibits both the wild-type and mutated forms of FLT3, AXL, ALK and LTK. This may result in an inhibition of FLT3-, AXL-, ALK-, and LTK-mediated signal transduction pathways and reduced proliferation in cancer cells that overexpress these RTKs. FLT3, AXL, ALK, and LTK, which are overexpressed or mutated in a variety of cancer cell types, play key roles in tumor cell growth and survival.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1819" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Hydrocortisone Sodium Succinate</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1819"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1819</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="The sodium salt of hydrocortisone succinate with glucocorticoid property. Hydrocortisone sodium succinate is chemically similar to the endogenous hormone that stimulates anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive activities, in addition to exhibiting minor mineralocorticoid effects. This agent binds to intracellular glucocorticoid receptors and is translocated into the nucleus, where it initiates the transcription of glucocorticoid-responsive genes, such as various cytokines and lipocortins. Lipocortins inhibit phospholipase A2, thereby blocking the release of arachidonic acid from membrane phospholipids and preventing the synthesis of prostaglandins and leukotrienes, both potent mediators of inflammation."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>The sodium salt of hydrocortisone succinate with glucocorticoid property. Hydrocortisone sodium succinate is chemically similar to the endogenous hormone that stimulates anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive activities, in addition to exhibiting minor mineralocorticoid effects. This agent binds to intracellular glucocorticoid receptors and is translocated into the nucleus, where it initiates the transcription of glucocorticoid-responsive genes, such as various cytokines and lipocortins. Lipocortins inhibit phospholipase A2, thereby blocking the release of arachidonic acid from membrane phospholipids and preventing the synthesis of prostaglandins and leukotrienes, both potent mediators of inflammation.</span></summary></details></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base gct hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Ifosfamide"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Ifosfamide" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C564" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Ifosfamide</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C564"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C564</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug that is used with other drugs to treat germ cell testicular cancer that did not respond to previous treatment with other drugs. It is also being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. Ifex attaches to DNA in cells and may kill cancer cells. It is a type of alkylating agent and a type of antimetabolite."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A drug that is used with other drugs to treat germ cell testicular cancer that did not respond to previous treatment with other drugs. It is also being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. Ifex attaches to DNA in cells and may kill cancer cells. It is a type of alkylating agent and a type of antimetabolite.</span></summary></details></td></tr>

Amethopterin stops cells from making DNA and may kill cancer cells. It is a type of antimetabolite."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A drug used to treat some types of cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, and severe skin conditions, such as psoriasis. Amethopterin stops cells from making DNA and may kill cancer cells. It is a type of antimetabolite.</span></summary></details></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Nitrogen Mustard"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Nitrogen Mustard" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C62056" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Nitrogen Mustard</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C62056"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C62056</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A synthetic agent related to sulphur mustard with antineoplastic and immunosuppressive properties. Nitrogen mustard (a member of a family of chemotherapy agents including cyclophosphamide and chlorambucil) is an irritant and carcinogenic agent metabolized to a highly reactive ethylene immonium derivative; the ethylene immonium derivative alkylates DNA and inhibits DNA replication. This agent also exhibits lympholytic properties. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A synthetic agent related to sulphur mustard with antineoplastic and immunosuppressive properties. Nitrogen mustard (a member of a family of chemotherapy agents including cyclophosphamide and chlorambucil) is an irritant and carcinogenic agent metabolized to a highly reactive ethylene immonium derivative; the ethylene immonium derivative alkylates DNA and inhibits DNA replication. This agent also exhibits lympholytic properties. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Nivolumab"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Nivolumab" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C68814" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Nivolumab</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C68814"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C68814</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A fully human immunoglobulin (Ig) G4 monoclonal antibody directed against the negative immunoregulatory human cell surface receptor programmed death-1 (PD-1, PCD-1) with immune checkpoint inhibitory and antineoplastic activities. Upon administration, nivolumab binds to and blocks the activation of PD-1, an immunoglobulin superfamily (IgSF) transmembrane protein, by its ligands programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1), which is overexpressed on certain cancer cells, and programmed cell death ligand 2 (PD-L2), which is primarily expressed on antigen-presenting cells (APCs). This results in the activation of T-cells and cell-mediated immune responses against tumor cells. Activated PD-1 negatively regulates T-cell activation and plays a key role in tumor evasion from host immunity."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A fully human immunoglobulin (Ig) G4 monoclonal antibody directed against the negative immunoregulatory human cell surface receptor programmed death-1 (PD-1, PCD-1) with immune checkpoint inhibitory and antineoplastic activities. Upon administration, nivolumab binds to and blocks the activation of PD-1, an immunoglobulin superfamily (IgSF) transmembrane protein, by its ligands programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1), which is overexpressed on certain cancer cells, and programmed cell death ligand 2 (PD-L2), which is primarily expressed on antigen-presenting cells (APCs). This results in the activation of T-cells and cell-mediated immune responses against tumor cells. Activated PD-1 negatively regulates T-cell activation and plays a key role in tumor evasion from host immunity.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Paclitaxel"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Paclitaxel" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1411" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Paclitaxel</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1411"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1411</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A compound extracted from the Pacific yew tree Taxus brevifolia with antineoplastic activity.  Paclitaxel binds to tubulin and inhibits the disassembly of microtubules, thereby resulting in the inhibition of cell division.  This agent also induces apoptosis by binding to and blocking the function of the apoptosis inhibitor protein Bcl-2 (B-cell Leukemia 2). (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A compound extracted from the Pacific yew tree Taxus brevifolia with antineoplastic activity.  Paclitaxel binds to tubulin and inhibits the disassembly of microtubules, thereby resulting in the inhibition of cell division.  This agent also induces apoptosis by binding to and blocking the function of the apoptosis inhibitor protein Bcl-2 (B-cell Leukemia 2). (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Pembroluzimab"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Pembroluzimab" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C106432" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Pembroluzimab</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C106432"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C106432</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A humanized monoclonal immunoglobulin (Ig) G4 antibody directed against human cell surface receptor PD-1 (programmed death-1 or programmed cell death-1) with potential immune checkpoint inhibitory and antineoplastic activities. Upon administration, pembrolizumab binds to PD-1, an inhibitory signaling receptor expressed on the surface of activated T cells, and blocks the binding to and activation of PD-1 by its ligands, which results in the activation of T-cell-mediated immune responses against tumor cells. The ligands for PD-1 include programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1), overexpressed on certain cancer cells, and programmed cell death ligand 2 (PD-L2), which is primarily expressed on APCs. Activated PD-1 negatively regulates T-cell activation and plays a key role in in tumor evasion from host immunity."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A humanized monoclonal immunoglobulin (Ig) G4 antibody directed against human cell surface receptor PD-1 (programmed death-1 or programmed cell death-1) with potential immune checkpoint inhibitory and antineoplastic activities. Upon administration, pembrolizumab binds to PD-1, an inhibitory signaling receptor expressed on the surface of activated T cells, and blocks the binding to and activation of PD-1 by its ligands, which results in the activation of T-cell-mediated immune responses against tumor cells. The ligands for PD-1 include programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1), overexpressed on certain cancer cells, and programmed cell death ligand 2 (PD-L2), which is primarily expressed on APCs. Activated PD-1 negatively regulates T-cell activation and plays a key role in in tumor evasion from host immunity.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Prednisone"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Prednisone" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C770" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Prednisone</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C770"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C770</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug used to lessen inflammation and lower the body's immune response. It is used with other drugs to treat leukemia and lymphoma and other types of cancer. It is also used alone or with other drugs to prevent or treat many other conditions. These include conditions related to cancer, such as anemia (a low level of red blood cells), allergic reactions, and loss of appetite. Prednisone is a type of therapeutic glucocorticoid."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A drug used to lessen inflammation and lower the body's immune response. It is used with other drugs to treat leukemia and lymphoma and other types of cancer. It is also used alone or with other drugs to prevent or treat many other conditions. These include conditions related to cancer, such as anemia (a low level of red blood cells), allergic reactions, and loss of appetite. Prednisone is a type of therapeutic glucocorticoid.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Procarbazine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Procarbazine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C62072" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Procarbazine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C62072"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C62072</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A methylhydrazine derivative with antineoplastic and mutagenic activities. Although the exact mode of cytotoxicity has not been elucidated, procarbazine, after metabolic activation, appears to inhibit the trans-methylation of methionine into transfer RNA (t-RNA), thereby preventing protein synthesis and consequently DNA and RNA synthesis. This agent may also undergo auto-oxidation, resulting in the formation of cytotoxic free radicals which damage DNA through an alkylation reaction."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A methylhydrazine derivative with antineoplastic and mutagenic activities. Although the exact mode of cytotoxicity has not been elucidated, procarbazine, after metabolic activation, appears to inhibit the trans-methylation of methionine into transfer RNA (t-RNA), thereby preventing protein synthesis and consequently DNA and RNA synthesis. This agent may also undergo auto-oxidation, resulting in the formation of cytotoxic free radicals which damage DNA through an alkylation reaction.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Quizartinib"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Quizartinib" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C68936" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Quizartinib</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C68936"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C68936</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title=""><details class="cell-details"><summary><span></span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Sorafenib"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Sorafenib" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C61948" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Sorafenib</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C61948"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C61948</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug used to treat advanced kidney cancer and a type of liver cancer that cannot be removed by surgery. It is also being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. Sorafenib stops cells from dividing and may prevent the growth of new blood vessels that tumors need to grow. It is a type of kinase inhibitor and a type of antiangiogenesis agent."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A drug used to treat advanced kidney cancer and a type of liver cancer that cannot be removed by surgery. It is also being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. Sorafenib stops cells from dividing and may prevent the growth of new blood vessels that tumors need to grow. It is a type of kinase inhibitor and a type of antiangiogenesis agent.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Thiotepa"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Thiotepa" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C875" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Thiotepa</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C875"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C875</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A polyfunctional, organophosphorus alkylating agent and a stable derivative of N,N',N''-triethylenephosphoramide (TEPA), with antineoplastic activity. Upon administration, thiotepa is converted into highly reactive ethylenimine groups, which covalently bind to nucleophilic groups in DNA and demonstrate a preference for the N7 position of guanine bases. This induces crosslinking of alkylated guanine bases in double-stranded DNA, interferes with both DNA replication and cell division, and results in both the induction of apoptosis and the inhibition of cell growth."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A polyfunctional, organophosphorus alkylating agent and a stable derivative of N,N',N''-triethylenephosphoramide (TEPA), with antineoplastic activity. Upon administration, thiotepa is converted into highly reactive ethylenimine groups, which covalently bind to nucleophilic groups in DNA and demonstrate a preference for the N7 position of guanine bases. This induces crosslinking of alkylated guanine bases in double-stranded DNA, interferes with both DNA replication and cell division, and results in both the induction of apoptosis and the inhibition of cell growth.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Tretinoin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Tretinoin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C900" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Tretinoin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C900"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C900</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A naturally-occurring acid of retinol. Tretinoin binds to and activates retinoic acid receptors (RARs), thereby inducing changes in gene expression that lead to cell differentiation, decreased cell proliferation, and inhibition of tumorigenesis.  This agent also inhibits telomerase, resulting in telomere shortening and eventual apoptosis of some tumor cell types.  The oral form of tretinoin has teratogenic and embryotoxic properties."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A naturally-occurring acid of retinol. Tretinoin binds to and activates retinoic acid receptors (RARs), thereby inducing changes in gene expression that lead to cell differentiation, decreased cell proliferation, and inhibition of tumorigenesis.  This agent also inhibits telomerase, resulting in telomere shortening and eventual apoptosis of some tumor cell types.  The oral form of tretinoin has teratogenic and embryotoxic properties.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Venoreline"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Venoreline" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1275" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Venoreline</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1275"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1275</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A semisynthetic vinca alkaloid. <tbody>
<tr data-subsets="base aml"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell Therapy"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell Therapy" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C126102" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell Therapy</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C126102"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C126102</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A type of treatment in which a patient's T cells (a type of immune system cell) are changed in the laboratory so they will attack cancer cells. T cells are taken from a patient's blood. Then the gene for a special receptor that binds to a certain protein on the patient's cancer cells is added in the laboratory. The special receptor is called a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR). Large numbers of the CAR T cells are grown in the laboratory and given to the patient by infusion. Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy is being studied in the treatment of some types of cancer."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A type of treatment in which a patient's T cells (a type of immune system cell) are changed in the laboratory so they will attack cancer cells. T cells are taken from a patient's blood. Then the gene for a special receptor that binds to a certain protein on the patient's cancer cells is added in the laboratory. The special receptor is called a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR). Large numbers of the CAR T cells are grown in the laboratory and given to the patient by infusion. Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy is being studied in the treatment of some types of cancer.</span></summary></details></td></tr>

Symptoms include the painless enlargement of lymph nodes, spleen, or other immune tissue. The two major types of Hodgkin lymphoma are classical Hodgkin lymphoma and nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma. NMRI is especially useful for imaging the brain, the spine, the soft tissue of joints, and the inside of bones.</span></summary></details></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Obstructive Lung Disease"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Obstructive Lung Disease" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3199" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Obstructive Lung Disease</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3199"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C3199</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A chronic and progressive lung disorder characterized by the loss of elasticity of the bronchial tree and the air sacs, destruction of the air sacs wall, thickening of the bronchial wall, and mucous accumulation in the bronchial tree. The pathologic changes result in the disruption of the air flow in the bronchial airways. Signs and symptoms include shortness of breath, wheezing, productive cough, and chest tightness. The two main types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are chronic obstructive bronchitis and emphysema."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A chronic and progressive lung disorder characterized by the loss of elasticity of the bronchial tree and the air sacs, destruction of the air sacs wall, thickening of the bronchial wall, and mucous accumulation in the bronchial tree. The pathologic changes result in the disruption of the air flow in the bronchial airways. Signs and symptoms include shortness of breath, wheezing, productive cough, and chest tightness. The two main types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are chronic obstructive bronchitis and emphysema.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Osteopenia"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Osteopenia" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C50910" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Osteopenia</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C50910"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C50910</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A condition in which there is a lower-than-normal bone mass or bone mineral density (the amount of bone mineral contained in a certain amount of bone). Osteopenia is a less severe form of bone loss than osteoporosis.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Osteoporosis"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Osteoporosis" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3298" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Osteoporosis</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3298"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C3298</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A condition of reduced bone mass, with decreased cortical thickness and a decrease in the number and size of the trabeculae of cancellous bone (but normal chemical composition), resulting in increased fracture incidence. Osteoporosis is classified as primary (Type 1, postmenopausal osteoporosis; Type 2, age-associated osteoporosis; and idiopathic, which can affect juveniles, premenopausal women, and middle-aged men) and secondary osteoporosis (which results from an identifiable cause of bone mass loss)."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A condition of reduced bone mass, with decreased cortical thickness and a decrease in the number and size of the trabeculae of cancellous bone (but normal chemical composition), resulting in increased fracture incidence. Osteoporosis is classified as primary (Type 1, postmenopausal osteoporosis; Type 2, age-associated osteoporosis; and idiopathic, which can affect juveniles, premenopausal women, and middle-aged men) and secondary osteoporosis (which results from an identifiable cause of bone mass loss).</span></summary></details></td></tr>

Causes of female infertility include endometriosis, fallopian tubes obstruction, and polycystic ovary syndrome. <tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C34415" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C34415"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C34415</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A complex syndrome resulting from various genetic and epigenetic anomalies of the 11p15.5 chromosomal region, leading to dysregulated expression of imprinted genes. Specific genes involved include CDKN1C, H19, IGF2, and KCNQ1OT1. One of the key genetic anomalies is an imbalance between the paternally expressed IGF2 growth enhancer gene and the maternally expressed H19 growth suppressor gene, leading to fetal and postnatal overgrowth. The condition is typically characterized by macrosomia, macroglossia, umbilical hernia or more severe abdominal wall anomalies such as omphalocele, ear lobe indentations, and hypoglycemia associated with hyperinsulinemia due to pancreatic islet cell hyperplasia. Patients with this syndrome have an increased risk for development of embryonal tumors (particularly Wilms tumor and hepatoblastoma) and adrenal cortex carcinoma."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A complex syndrome resulting from various genetic and epigenetic anomalies of the 11p15.5 chromosomal region, leading to dysregulated expression of imprinted genes. Specific genes involved include CDKN1C, H19, IGF2, and KCNQ1OT1. One of the key genetic anomalies is an imbalance between the paternally expressed IGF2 growth enhancer gene and the maternally expressed H19 growth suppressor gene, leading to fetal and postnatal overgrowth. The condition is typically characterized by macrosomia, macroglossia, umbilical hernia or more severe abdominal wall anomalies such as omphalocele, ear lobe indentations, and hypoglycemia associated with hyperinsulinemia due to pancreatic islet cell hyperplasia. Patients with this syndrome have an increased risk for development of embryonal tumors (particularly Wilms tumor and hepatoblastoma) and adrenal cortex carcinoma.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Celiac Disease"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Celiac Disease" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C26714" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Celiac Disease</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C26714"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C26714</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A digestive disease that is caused by an immune response to a protein called gluten, which is found in wheat, rye, barley, and oats. Celiac disease damages the lining of the small intestine and interferes with the absorption of nutrients from food. A person with celiac disease may become malnourished no matter how much food is consumed."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A digestive disease that is caused by an immune response to a protein called gluten, which is found in wheat, rye, barley, and oats. Celiac disease damages the lining of the small intestine and interferes with the absorption of nutrients from food. A person with celiac disease may become malnourished no matter how much food is consumed.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Central Hypoventilation Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Central Hypoventilation Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C98889" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Central Hypoventilation Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C98889"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C98889</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A disorder characterized by hypoventilation and hypoxemia. <tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Cleft Lip"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Cleft Lip" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C87175" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Cleft Lip</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C87175"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C87175</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A congenital abnormality consisting of one or more clefts (splits) in the upper lip, which may be accompanied by a cleft palate; it is the result of the failure of the embryonic parts of the lip to fuse."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A congenital abnormality consisting of one or more clefts (splits) in the upper lip, which may be accompanied by a cleft palate; it is the result of the failure of the embryonic parts of the lip to fuse.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Cleft Palate"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Cleft Palate" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C87069" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Cleft Palate</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C87069"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C87069</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A congenital abnormality consisting of a fissure in the midline of the hard and/or soft palate; it is the result of the failure of the two sides of the palate to fuse during embryonic development."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A congenital abnormality consisting of a fissure in the midline of the hard and/or soft palate; it is the result of the failure of the two sides of the palate to fuse during embryonic development.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
