<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Costello Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Costello Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C84652" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Costello Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C84652"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C84652</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A genetic syndrome caused by mutations in the HRAS gene. It is characterized by developmental delay, mental retardation, loose skin folds, cardiomyopathy, tachycardia, and structural heart defects. Patients are at an increased risk of developing benign or malignant neoplasms."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A genetic syndrome caused by mutations in the HRAS gene. It is characterized by developmental delay, mental retardation, loose skin folds, cardiomyopathy, tachycardia, and structural heart defects. Patients are at an increased risk of developing benign or malignant neoplasms.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Cushing Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Cushing Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C2969" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Cushing Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C2969"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C2969</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A clinical condition characterized by variable degrees of central obesity, rounding of the face (&quot;moon&quot; face), hypertension, striae, and a number of other physical findings, as a result of prolonged exposure to supranormal cortisol concentration of any etiology."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A clinical condition characterized by variable degrees of central obesity, rounding of the face ("moon" face), hypertension, striae, and a number of other physical findings, as a result of prolonged exposure to supranormal cortisol concentration of any etiology.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Denys-Drash Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Denys-Drash Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C84668" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Denys-Drash Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C84668"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C84668</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A Wilms tumor 1 gene syndrome caused by various point mutation(s) affecting the zinc finger(s) of the Wilms tumor protein. This syndrome is characterized by congenital nephropathy (diffuse mesangial sclerosis), gonadal dysgenesis resulting in atypical genital and reproductive tract development in male infants, and high risk for development of Wilms tumor, an embryonal neoplasm defined by the presence of epithelial, mesenchymal, and blastema components."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A Wilms tumor 1 gene syndrome caused by various point mutation(s) affecting the zinc finger(s) of the Wilms tumor protein. This syndrome is characterized by congenital nephropathy (diffuse mesangial sclerosis), gonadal dysgenesis resulting in atypical genital and reproductive tract development in male infants, and high risk for development of Wilms tumor, an embryonal neoplasm defined by the presence of epithelial, mesenchymal, and blastema components.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Diabetes Mellitus (Type I)"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Diabetes Mellitus (Type I)" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C2986" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Diabetes Mellitus (Type I)</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C2986"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C2986</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A chronic condition characterized by minimal or absent production of insulin by the pancreas."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A chronic condition characterized by minimal or absent production of insulin by the pancreas.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base nrsts"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="DICER1"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="DICER1" data-pv-meaning="" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>DICER1</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title=""><span></span></td><td class="enum-description" title=""><details class="cell-details"><summary><span></span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Down Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Down Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C2993" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Down Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C2993"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C2993</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A chromosomal dysgenesis syndrome resulting from a triplication or translocation of chromosome 21. Down syndrome occurs in approximately 1:700 live births. Abnormalities are variable from individual to individual and may include mental retardation, retarded growth, flat hypoplastic face with short nose, prominent epicanthic skin folds, small low-set ears with prominent antihelix, fissured and thickened tongue, laxness of joint ligaments, pelvic dysplasia, broad hands and feet, stubby fingers, transverse palmar crease, lenticular opacities and heart disease. Patients with Down syndrome have an estimated 10 to 30-fold increased risk for leukemia; most have symptoms of Alzheimer's disease by age 40. Also known as trisomy 21 syndrome."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A chromosomal dysgenesis syndrome resulting from a triplication or translocation of chromosome 21. Down syndrome occurs in approximately 1:700 live births. Abnormalities are variable from individual to individual and may include mental retardation, retarded growth, flat hypoplastic face with short nose, prominent epicanthic skin folds, small low-set ears with prominent antihelix, fissured and thickened tongue, laxness of joint ligaments, pelvic dysplasia, broad hands and feet, stubby fingers, transverse palmar crease, lenticular opacities and heart disease. Patients with Down syndrome have an estimated 10 to 30-fold increased risk for leukemia; most have symptoms of Alzheimer's disease by age 40. Also known as trisomy 21 syndrome.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Frasier Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Frasier Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C122805" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Frasier Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C122805"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C122805</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title=""><details class="cell-details"><summary><span></span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Gastroschisis"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Gastroschisis" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C84725" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Gastroschisis</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C84725"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C84725</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A congenital birth defect characterized by the exposure of the fetal intestines outside the abdominal wall through an abdominal wall opening."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A congenital birth defect characterized by the exposure of the fetal intestines outside the abdominal wall through an abdominal wall opening.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Gonadal Dysgenesis"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Gonadal Dysgenesis" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C61420" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Gonadal Dysgenesis</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C61420"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C61420</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title=""><details class="cell-details"><summary><span></span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Goodpasture's Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Goodpasture's Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C34649" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Goodpasture's Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C34649"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C34649</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autoimmune disorder characterized by pulmonary hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis. It is a hypersensitivity reaction resulting in the formation of antibodies against the pulmonary alveoli and the basement membrane of the glomeruli."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autoimmune disorder characterized by pulmonary hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis. It is a hypersensitivity reaction resulting in the formation of antibodies against the pulmonary alveoli and the basement membrane of the glomeruli.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Gorlin Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Gorlin Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C2892" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Gorlin Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C2892"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C2892</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A genetic condition that causes unusual facial features and disorders of the skin, bones, nervous system, eyes, and endocrine glands. People with this syndrome have a higher risk of basal cell carcinoma."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A genetic condition that causes unusual facial features and disorders of the skin, bones, nervous system, eyes, and endocrine glands. People with this syndrome have a higher risk of basal cell carcinoma.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Graves' Disease"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Graves' Disease" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3071" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Graves' Disease</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3071"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C3071</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autoimmune condition characterized by excessive immunoglobulin stimulation of the thyroid gland resulting in hyperthyroidism."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autoimmune condition characterized by excessive immunoglobulin stimulation of the thyroid gland resulting in hyperthyroidism.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Hashimoto's Thyroiditis"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Hashimoto's Thyroiditis" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C27191" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Hashimoto's Thyroiditis</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C27191"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C27191</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autoimmune condition of the thyroid gland (a gland located beneath the larynx). It is caused by the formation of antibodies that attack the thyroid gland and it usually causes hypothyroidism (too little thyroid hormone). Symptoms include fatigue, weight gain, constipation, dry skin, depression, and the inability to exercise. It is more common in females and can run in families."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autoimmune condition of the thyroid gland (a gland located beneath the larynx). It is caused by the formation of antibodies that attack the thyroid gland and it usually causes hypothyroidism (too little thyroid hormone). Symptoms include fatigue, weight gain, constipation, dry skin, depression, and the inability to exercise. It is more common in females and can run in families.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Heart Defect"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Heart Defect" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C168217" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Heart Defect</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C168217"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C168217</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="Genetic anomalies and collections of malformations that are known to cluster together that can be associated with congenital heart defects."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Genetic anomalies and collections of malformations that are known to cluster together that can be associated with congenital heart defects.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Hemihypertrophy"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Hemihypertrophy" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C88541" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Hemihypertrophy</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C88541"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C88541</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A condition in which one side of the body or a part of one side is larger than the other. Children with hemihypertrophy have an increased risk of developing certain types of cancer, including Wilms tumor (a childhood kidney cancer) and liver cancer."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A condition in which one side of the body or a part of one side is larger than the other. Children with hemihypertrophy have an increased risk of developing certain types of cancer, including Wilms tumor (a childhood kidney cancer) and liver cancer.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Hereditary Retinoblastoma"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Hereditary Retinoblastoma" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C8495" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Hereditary Retinoblastoma</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C8495"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C8495</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An inherited malignant tumor that originates in the nuclear layer of the retina. A predisposition to retinoblastoma has been associated with 13q14 cytogenetic abnormalities affecting the RB1 gene. Patients with the inherited form appear to be at increased risk for secondary non-ocular malignancies such as osteosarcoma, malignant fibrous histiocytoma, and fibrosarcoma."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An inherited malignant tumor that originates in the nuclear layer of the retina. A predisposition to retinoblastoma has been associated with 13q14 cytogenetic abnormalities affecting the RB1 gene. Patients with the inherited form appear to be at increased risk for secondary non-ocular malignancies such as osteosarcoma, malignant fibrous histiocytoma, and fibrosarcoma.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Hirschsprung Disease"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Hirschsprung Disease" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C34700" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Hirschsprung Disease</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C34700"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C34700</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A congenital disorder characterized by the absence of ganglion cells usually in the rectosigmoid colon (short segment Hirschsprung disease) or, rarely, throughout the entire colon and small bowel (total intestinal aganglionosis)."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A congenital disorder characterized by the absence of ganglion cells usually in the rectosigmoid colon (short segment Hirschsprung disease) or, rarely, throughout the entire colon and small bowel (total intestinal aganglionosis).</span></summary></details></td></tr>

Inflammatory bowel disease includes ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease.</span></summary></details></td></tr>

The condition is characterized in childhood by relative tall stature with disproportionately long limbs, and speech/language developmental problems in some patients. Postpubertal findings include small testes, gynecomastia, and infertility."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A condition caused by the presence of an extra X chromosome resulting in 47,XXY karyotype in an individual with male phenotype. The condition is characterized in childhood by relative tall stature with disproportionately long limbs, and speech/language developmental problems in some patients. Postpubertal findings include small testes, gynecomastia, and infertility.</span></summary></details></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Lynch Syndrome"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Lynch Syndrome" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C8494" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Lynch Syndrome</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C8494"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C8494</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autosomal dominant hereditary neoplastic syndrome characterized by the development of colorectal carcinoma and a high risk of developing endometrial carcinoma, gastric carcinoma, ovarian carcinoma, renal pelvis carcinoma, and small intestinal carcinoma. Patients often develop colorectal carcinomas at an early age (mean, 45 years). In the majority of the cases the lesions arise from the proximal colon. At the molecular level, high-frequency microsatellite instability is present."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autosomal dominant hereditary neoplastic syndrome characterized by the development of colorectal carcinoma and a high risk of developing endometrial carcinoma, gastric carcinoma, ovarian carcinoma, renal pelvis carcinoma, and small intestinal carcinoma. Patients often develop colorectal carcinomas at an early age (mean, 45 years). In the majority of the cases the lesions arise from the proximal colon. At the molecular level, high-frequency microsatellite instability is present.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Mixed Connective Tissue Disease"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Mixed Connective Tissue Disease" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C84892" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Mixed Connective Tissue Disease</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C84892"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C84892</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An autoimmune disorder which is associated with high titer anti-RNP antibody, and usually features Raynaud's Phenomenon and swollen fingers."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An autoimmune disorder which is associated with high titer anti-RNP antibody, and usually features Raynaud's Phenomenon and swollen fingers.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Multiple Sclerosis"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Multiple Sclerosis" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C3243" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Multiple Sclerosis</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C3243"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C3243</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A disorder of the central nervous system marked by weakness, numbness, a loss of muscle coordination, and problems with vision, speech, and bladder control. Multiple sclerosis is thought to be an autoimmune disease in which the body's immune system destroys myelin. Myelin is a substance that contains both protein and fat (lipid), serving as a nerve insulator and helping in the transmission of nerve signals."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A disorder of the central nervous system marked by weakness, numbness, a loss of muscle coordination, and problems with vision, speech, and bladder control. Multiple sclerosis is thought to be an autoimmune disease in which the body's immune system destroys myelin. Myelin is a substance that contains both protein and fat (lipid), serving as a nerve insulator and helping in the transmission of nerve signals.</span></summary></details></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Bleomycin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Bleomycin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C313" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Bleomycin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C313"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C313</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A mixture of glycopeptide antineoplastic antibiotics isolated from the bacterium Streptomyces verticillus. Bleomycin forms complexes with iron that reduce molecular oxygen to superoxide and hydroxyl radicals which cause single- and double-stranded breaks in DNA; these reactive oxygen species also induce lipid peroxidation, carbohydrate oxidation, and alterations in prostaglandin synthesis and degradation."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A mixture of glycopeptide antineoplastic antibiotics isolated from the bacterium Streptomyces verticillus. Bleomycin forms complexes with iron that reduce molecular oxygen to superoxide and hydroxyl radicals which cause single- and double-stranded breaks in DNA; these reactive oxygen species also induce lipid peroxidation, carbohydrate oxidation, and alterations in prostaglandin synthesis and degradation.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Brentuximab Vedotin"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Brentuximab Vedotin" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C66944" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Brentuximab Vedotin</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C66944"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C66944</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="An antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) directed against the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) receptor CD30 with potential antineoplastic activity. Brentuximab vedotin is generated by conjugating the chimeric anti-CD30 monoclonal antibody SGN-30 to the cytotoxic agent monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via a valine-citrulline peptide linker. Upon administration and internalization by CD30-positive tumor cells, brentuximab vedotin undergoes enzymatic cleavage, releasing MMAE into the cytosol; MMAE binds to tubulin and inhibits tubulin polymerization, which may result in G2/M phase arrest and tumor cell apoptosis. Transiently activated during lymphocyte activation, CD30 (tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily, member 8;TNFRSF8) may be constitutively expressed in hematologic malignancies including Hodgkin lymphoma and some T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas. The linkage system in brentuximab vedotin is highly stable in plasma, resulting in cytotoxic specificity for CD30-positive cells."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>An antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) directed against the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) receptor CD30 with potential antineoplastic activity. Brentuximab vedotin is generated by conjugating the chimeric anti-CD30 monoclonal antibody SGN-30 to the cytotoxic agent monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via a valine-citrulline peptide linker. Upon administration and internalization by CD30-positive tumor cells, brentuximab vedotin undergoes enzymatic cleavage, releasing MMAE into the cytosol; MMAE binds to tubulin and inhibits tubulin polymerization, which may result in G2/M phase arrest and tumor cell apoptosis. Transiently activated during lymphocyte activation, CD30 (tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily, member 8;TNFRSF8) may be constitutively expressed in hematologic malignancies including Hodgkin lymphoma and some T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas. The linkage system in brentuximab vedotin is highly stable in plasma, resulting in cytotoxic specificity for CD30-positive cells.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Busulfan"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Busulfan" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C321" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Busulfan</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C321"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C321</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A synthetic derivative of dimethane-sulfonate with antineoplastic and cytotoxic properties.  Although its mechanism of action is not fully understood, busulfan appears to act through the alkylation of DNA.  Following systemic absorption of busulfan, carbonium ions are formed, resulting in DNA alkylation and DNA breaks and inhibition of DNA replication and RNA transcription. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A synthetic derivative of dimethane-sulfonate with antineoplastic and cytotoxic properties.  Although its mechanism of action is not fully understood, busulfan appears to act through the alkylation of DNA.  Following systemic absorption of busulfan, carbonium ions are formed, resulting in DNA alkylation and DNA breaks and inhibition of DNA replication and RNA transcription. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>

It is also used with other drugs to treat advanced, metastatic, or recurrent non-small cell lung cancer and is being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. Paraplatin is a form of the anticancer drug cisplatin and causes fewer side effects in patients. It attaches to DNA in cells and may kill cancer cells. It is a type of platinum compound."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A drug that is used to treat advanced ovarian cancer that has never been treated or symptoms of ovarian cancer that has come back after treatment with other anticancer drugs. It is also used with other drugs to treat advanced, metastatic, or recurrent non-small cell lung cancer and is being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. Paraplatin is a form of the anticancer drug cisplatin and causes fewer side effects in patients. It attaches to DNA in cells and may kill cancer cells. It is a type of platinum compound.</span></summary></details></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Fludarabine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Fludarabine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1094" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Fludarabine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1094"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1094</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A fluorinated nucleotide antimetabolite analog of the antiviral agent vidarabine (ara-A) with antineoplastic activity. Administered parenterally as a phosphate salt, fludarabine phosphate is rapidly dephosphorylated to 2-fluoro-ara-A and then phosphorylated intracellularly by deoxycytidine kinase to the active triphosphate, 2-fluoro-ara-ATP. This metabolite may inhibit DNA polymerase alpha, ribonucleotide reductase and DNA primase, thereby interrupting DNA synthesis and inhibiting tumor cell growth.  (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A fluorinated nucleotide antimetabolite analog of the antiviral agent vidarabine (ara-A) with antineoplastic activity. Administered parenterally as a phosphate salt, fludarabine phosphate is rapidly dephosphorylated to 2-fluoro-ara-A and then phosphorylated intracellularly by deoxycytidine kinase to the active triphosphate, 2-fluoro-ara-ATP. This metabolite may inhibit DNA polymerase alpha, ribonucleotide reductase and DNA primase, thereby interrupting DNA synthesis and inhibiting tumor cell growth.  (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Gemcitabine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Gemcitabine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C66876" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Gemcitabine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C66876"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C66876</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A broad-spectrum antimetabolite and deoxycytidine analogue with antineoplastic activity. Upon administration, gemcitabine is converted into the active metabolites difluorodeoxycytidine diphosphate (dFdCDP) and difluorodeoxycytidine triphosphate (dFdCTP) by deoxycytidine kinase. dFdCTP competes with deoxycytidine triphosphate (dCTP) and is incorporated into DNA.  This locks DNA polymerase thereby resulting in &quot;masked termination&quot; during DNA replication. On the other hand, dFdCDP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, thereby decreasing the deoxynucleotide pool available for DNA synthesis. The reduction in the intracellular concentration of dCTP potentiates the incorporation of dFdCTP into DNA."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A broad-spectrum antimetabolite and deoxycytidine analogue with antineoplastic activity. Upon administration, gemcitabine is converted into the active metabolites difluorodeoxycytidine diphosphate (dFdCDP) and difluorodeoxycytidine triphosphate (dFdCTP) by deoxycytidine kinase. dFdCTP competes with deoxycytidine triphosphate (dCTP) and is incorporated into DNA.  This locks DNA polymerase thereby resulting in "masked termination" during DNA replication. On the other hand, dFdCDP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, thereby decreasing the deoxynucleotide pool available for DNA synthesis. The reduction in the intracellular concentration of dCTP potentiates the incorporation of dFdCTP into DNA.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Ifosfamide"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Ifosfamide" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C564" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Ifosfamide</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C564"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C564</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug that is used with other drugs to treat germ cell testicular cancer that did not respond to previous treatment with other drugs. It is a type of alkylating agent and a type of antimetabolite.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Melphalan"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Melphalan" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C633" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Melphalan</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C633"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C633</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug that is used to treat multiple myeloma and ovarian epithelial cancer and is being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer. <tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Methotrexate"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Methotrexate" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C642" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Methotrexate</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C642"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C642</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug used to treat some types of cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, and severe skin conditions, such as psoriasis. Amethopterin stops cells from making DNA and may kill cancer cells. It is a type of antimetabolite."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A drug used to treat some types of cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, and severe skin conditions, such as psoriasis. Amethopterin stops cells from making DNA and may kill cancer cells. It is a type of antimetabolite.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Nitrogen Mustard"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Nitrogen Mustard" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C62056" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Nitrogen Mustard</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C62056"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C62056</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A synthetic agent related to sulphur mustard with antineoplastic and immunosuppressive properties. Nitrogen mustard (a member of a family of chemotherapy agents including cyclophosphamide and chlorambucil) is an irritant and carcinogenic agent metabolized to a highly reactive ethylene immonium derivative; the ethylene immonium derivative alkylates DNA and inhibits DNA replication. This agent also exhibits lympholytic properties. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A synthetic agent related to sulphur mustard with antineoplastic and immunosuppressive properties. Nitrogen mustard (a member of a family of chemotherapy agents including cyclophosphamide and chlorambucil) is an irritant and carcinogenic agent metabolized to a highly reactive ethylene immonium derivative; the ethylene immonium derivative alkylates DNA and inhibits DNA replication. This agent also exhibits lympholytic properties. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Nivolumab"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Nivolumab" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C68814" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Nivolumab</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C68814"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C68814</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A fully human immunoglobulin (Ig) G4 monoclonal antibody directed against the negative immunoregulatory human cell surface receptor programmed death-1 (PD-1, PCD-1) with immune checkpoint inhibitory and antineoplastic activities. Upon administration, nivolumab binds to and blocks the activation of PD-1, an immunoglobulin superfamily (IgSF) transmembrane protein, by its ligands programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1), which is overexpressed on certain cancer cells, and programmed cell death ligand 2 (PD-L2), which is primarily expressed on antigen-presenting cells (APCs). This results in the activation of T-cells and cell-mediated immune responses against tumor cells. Activated PD-1 negatively regulates T-cell activation and plays a key role in tumor evasion from host immunity."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A fully human immunoglobulin (Ig) G4 monoclonal antibody directed against the negative immunoregulatory human cell surface receptor programmed death-1 (PD-1, PCD-1) with immune checkpoint inhibitory and antineoplastic activities. Upon administration, nivolumab binds to and blocks the activation of PD-1, an immunoglobulin superfamily (IgSF) transmembrane protein, by its ligands programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1), which is overexpressed on certain cancer cells, and programmed cell death ligand 2 (PD-L2), which is primarily expressed on antigen-presenting cells (APCs). This results in the activation of T-cells and cell-mediated immune responses against tumor cells. Activated PD-1 negatively regulates T-cell activation and plays a key role in tumor evasion from host immunity.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Pembrolizumab"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Pembrolizumab" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C106432" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Pembrolizumab</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C106432"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C106432</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A humanized monoclonal immunoglobulin (Ig) G4 antibody directed against human cell surface receptor PD-1 (programmed death-1 or programmed cell death-1) with potential immune checkpoint inhibitory and antineoplastic activities. Upon administration, pembrolizumab binds to PD-1, an inhibitory signaling receptor expressed on the surface of activated T cells, and blocks the binding to and activation of PD-1 by its ligands, which results in the activation of T-cell-mediated immune responses against tumor cells. The ligands for PD-1 include programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1), overexpressed on certain cancer cells, and programmed cell death ligand 2 (PD-L2), which is primarily expressed on APCs. Activated PD-1 negatively regulates T-cell activation and plays a key role in in tumor evasion from host immunity."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A humanized monoclonal immunoglobulin (Ig) G4 antibody directed against human cell surface receptor PD-1 (programmed death-1 or programmed cell death-1) with potential immune checkpoint inhibitory and antineoplastic activities. Upon administration, pembrolizumab binds to PD-1, an inhibitory signaling receptor expressed on the surface of activated T cells, and blocks the binding to and activation of PD-1 by its ligands, which results in the activation of T-cell-mediated immune responses against tumor cells. The ligands for PD-1 include programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1), overexpressed on certain cancer cells, and programmed cell death ligand 2 (PD-L2), which is primarily expressed on APCs. Activated PD-1 negatively regulates T-cell activation and plays a key role in in tumor evasion from host immunity.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Prednisone"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Prednisone" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C770" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Prednisone</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C770"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C770</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A drug used to lessen inflammation and lower the body's immune response. It is used with other drugs to treat leukemia and lymphoma and other types of cancer. It is also used alone or with other drugs to prevent or treat many other conditions. These include conditions related to cancer, such as anemia (a low level of red blood cells), allergic reactions, and loss of appetite. Prednisone is a type of therapeutic glucocorticoid."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A drug used to lessen inflammation and lower the body's immune response. It is used with other drugs to treat leukemia and lymphoma and other types of cancer. It is also used alone or with other drugs to prevent or treat many other conditions. These include conditions related to cancer, such as anemia (a low level of red blood cells), allergic reactions, and loss of appetite. Prednisone is a type of therapeutic glucocorticoid.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Procarbazine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Procarbazine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C62072" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Procarbazine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C62072"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C62072</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A methylhydrazine derivative with antineoplastic and mutagenic activities. Although the exact mode of cytotoxicity has not been elucidated, procarbazine, after metabolic activation, appears to inhibit the trans-methylation of methionine into transfer RNA (t-RNA), thereby preventing protein synthesis and consequently DNA and RNA synthesis. This agent may also undergo auto-oxidation, resulting in the formation of cytotoxic free radicals which damage DNA through an alkylation reaction."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A methylhydrazine derivative with antineoplastic and mutagenic activities. Although the exact mode of cytotoxicity has not been elucidated, procarbazine, after metabolic activation, appears to inhibit the trans-methylation of methionine into transfer RNA (t-RNA), thereby preventing protein synthesis and consequently DNA and RNA synthesis. This agent may also undergo auto-oxidation, resulting in the formation of cytotoxic free radicals which damage DNA through an alkylation reaction.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Thiotepa"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Thiotepa" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C875" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Thiotepa</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C875"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C875</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A polyfunctional, organophosphorus alkylating agent and a stable derivative of N,N',N''-triethylenephosphoramide (TEPA), with antineoplastic activity. Upon administration, thiotepa is converted into highly reactive ethylenimine groups, which covalently bind to nucleophilic groups in DNA and demonstrate a preference for the N7 position of guanine bases. This induces crosslinking of alkylated guanine bases in double-stranded DNA, interferes with both DNA replication and cell division, and results in both the induction of apoptosis and the inhibition of cell growth."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A polyfunctional, organophosphorus alkylating agent and a stable derivative of N,N',N''-triethylenephosphoramide (TEPA), with antineoplastic activity. Upon administration, thiotepa is converted into highly reactive ethylenimine groups, which covalently bind to nucleophilic groups in DNA and demonstrate a preference for the N7 position of guanine bases. This induces crosslinking of alkylated guanine bases in double-stranded DNA, interferes with both DNA replication and cell division, and results in both the induction of apoptosis and the inhibition of cell growth.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Vinblastine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Vinblastine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C930" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Vinblastine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C930"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C930</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A natural alkaloid isolated from the plant Vinca rosea Linn. Vinblastine binds to tubulin and inhibits microtubule formation, resulting in disruption of mitotic spindle assembly and arrest of tumor cells in the M phase of the cell cycle. This agent may also interfere with amino acid, cyclic AMP, and glutathione metabolism; calmodulin-dependent Ca++ -transport ATPase activity; cellular respiration; and nucleic acid and lipid biosynthesis. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A natural alkaloid isolated from the plant Vinca rosea Linn. Vinblastine binds to tubulin and inhibits microtubule formation, resulting in disruption of mitotic spindle assembly and arrest of tumor cells in the M phase of the cell cycle. This agent may also interfere with amino acid, cyclic AMP, and glutathione metabolism; calmodulin-dependent Ca++ -transport ATPase activity; cellular respiration; and nucleic acid and lipid biosynthesis. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Vincristine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Vincristine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C933" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Vincristine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C933"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C933</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A natural alkaloid isolated from the plant Vinca rosea Linn. Vincristine binds irreversibly to microtubules and spindle proteins in S phase of the cell cycle and interferes with the formation of the mitotic spindle, thereby arresting tumor cells in metaphase. This agent also depolymerizes microtubules and may also interfere with amino acid, cyclic AMP, and glutathione metabolism; calmodulin-dependent Ca++ -transport ATPase activity; cellular respiration; and nucleic acid and lipid biosynthesis. (NCI04)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A natural alkaloid isolated from the plant Vinca rosea Linn. Vincristine binds irreversibly to microtubules and spindle proteins in S phase of the cell cycle and interferes with the formation of the mitotic spindle, thereby arresting tumor cells in metaphase. This agent also depolymerizes microtubules and may also interfere with amino acid, cyclic AMP, and glutathione metabolism; calmodulin-dependent Ca++ -transport ATPase activity; cellular respiration; and nucleic acid and lipid biosynthesis. (NCI04)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Vinorelbine"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Vinorelbine" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C1275" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Vinorelbine</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C1275"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C1275</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A semisynthetic vinca alkaloid. Vinorelbine binds to tubulin and prevents formation of the mitotic spindle, resulting in the arrest of tumor cell growth in metaphase. This agent may also interfere with amino acid, cyclic AMP. and glutathione metabolism; calmodulin-dependent Ca++ -transport ATPase activity; cellular respiration; and nucleic acid and lipid biosynthesis."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A semisynthetic vinca alkaloid. Vinorelbine binds to tubulin and prevents formation of the mitotic spindle, resulting in the arrest of tumor cell growth in metaphase. This agent may also interfere with amino acid, cyclic AMP. and glutathione metabolism; calmodulin-dependent Ca++ -transport ATPase activity; cellular respiration; and nucleic acid and lipid biosynthesis.</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Other"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Other" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C17649" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Other</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C17649"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C17649</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="A proper value is applicable but not known."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A proper value is applicable but not known.</span></summary></details></td></tr>

NOTE: Four categories of discontinuation are distinguished: a) dropout: Active discontinuation by a subject (also a noun referring to such a discontinued subject); b) investigator initiated discontinuation (e.g., for cause); c) loss to follow-up: cessation of participation without notice or action by the subject; d) sponsor initiated discontinuation. Note that subject discontinuation does not necessarily imply exclusion of subject data from analysis. &quot;Termination of subject&quot; has a history of synonymous use, but is now considered nonstandard. [After ICH E3, section 10.1 and FDA Guidance for Industry: Submission of Abbreviated Reports &amp; Synopses in Support of Marketing Applications, IV A] (CDISC Glossary)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>The act of concluding participation by an enrolled subject prior to completion of all protocol-required elements in a study. NOTE: Four categories of discontinuation are distinguished: a) dropout: Active discontinuation by a subject (also a noun referring to such a discontinued subject); b) investigator initiated discontinuation (e.g., for cause); c) loss to follow-up: cessation of participation without notice or action by the subject; d) sponsor initiated discontinuation. Note that subject discontinuation does not necessarily imply exclusion of subject data from analysis. "Termination of subject" has a history of synonymous use, but is now considered nonstandard. [After ICH E3, section 10.1 and FDA Guidance for Industry: Submission of Abbreviated Reports & Synopses in Support of Marketing Applications, IV A] (CDISC Glossary)</span></summary></details></td></tr>

Peripheral blood stem cell transplantation (PBSCT) is used for the treatment of certain blood disorders, following partial or complete bone marrow ablation, or following high dose chemotherapy or radiation treatment for cancer. Immature circulating blood cells, similar to stem cells in the bone marrow, are removed before treatment. The cells are then given to the patient after treatment to help the bone marrow recover and continue producing healthy blood cells. Transplantation may be autologous (the patient's own blood cells are used), allogeneic (blood cells are donated by someone else), or syngeneic (blood cells are donated by an identical twin)."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>A method of hematopoietic reconstitution utilizing stem cells harvested from the circulating blood of a patient or donor. Peripheral blood stem cell transplantation (PBSCT) is used for the treatment of certain blood disorders, following partial or complete bone marrow ablation, or following high dose chemotherapy or radiation treatment for cancer. Immature circulating blood cells, similar to stem cells in the bone marrow, are removed before treatment. The cells are then given to the patient after treatment to help the bone marrow recover and continue producing healthy blood cells. Transplantation may be autologous (the patient's own blood cells are used), allogeneic (blood cells are donated by someone else), or syngeneic (blood cells are donated by an identical twin).</span></summary></details></td></tr>

<tr data-subsets="base gct"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Stage IA"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Stage IA" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C6361" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Stage IA</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C6361"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C6361</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="Stage IA includes: pT1, N0, M0, S0.  pT1: Tumor limited to the testis and epididymis without vascular/lymphatic invasion; tumor may invade into the tunica albuginea but not the tunica vaginalis.  N0: No regional lymph node metastasis.  M0: No distant metastasis.  S0: Marker study levels within normal limits. (AJCC 6th and 7th eds.)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Stage IA includes: pT1, N0, M0, S0.  pT1: Tumor limited to the testis and epididymis without vascular/lymphatic invasion; tumor may invade into the tunica albuginea but not the tunica vaginalis.  N0: No regional lymph node metastasis.  M0: No distant metastasis.  S0: Marker study levels within normal limits. (AJCC 6th and 7th eds.)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Stage IB"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Stage IB" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C6362" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Stage IB</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C6362"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C6362</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="Stage IB includes: (pT2, N0, M0, S0); (pT3, N0, M0, S0); (pT4, N0, M0, S0).  pT2: Tumor limited to the testis and epididymis with vascular/lymphatic invasion, or tumor extending through the tunica albuginea with involvement of the tunica vaginalis.  pT3: Tumor invades the spermatic cord with or without vascular/lymphatic invasion.  pT4: Tumor invades the scrotum with or without vascular/lymphatic invasion.  N0: No regional lymph node metastasis.  M0: No distant metastasis.  S0: Marker study levels within normal limits. (AJCC 6th and 7th eds.)"><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Stage IB includes: (pT2, N0, M0, S0); (pT3, N0, M0, S0); (pT4, N0, M0, S0).  pT2: Tumor limited to the testis and epididymis with vascular/lymphatic invasion, or tumor extending through the tunica albuginea with involvement of the tunica vaginalis.  pT3: Tumor invades the spermatic cord with or without vascular/lymphatic invasion.  pT4: Tumor invades the scrotum with or without vascular/lymphatic invasion.  N0: No regional lymph node metastasis.  M0: No distant metastasis.  S0: Marker study levels within normal limits. (AJCC 6th and 7th eds.)</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct hl"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Stage II"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Stage II" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C8116" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Stage II</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C8116"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C8116</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="Ann Arbor Classification: Stage II: Involvement of two or more lymph node regions on the same side of the diaphragm (II); or localized involvement of a single extralymphatic organ or site in association with regional lymph node involvement with or without involvement of other lymph node regions on the same side of the diaphragm (IIE)."><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Ann Arbor Classification: Stage II: Involvement of two or more lymph node regions on the same side of the diaphragm (II); or localized involvement of a single extralymphatic organ or site in association with regional lymph node involvement with or without involvement of other lymph node regions on the same side of the diaphragm (IIE).</span></summary></details></td></tr>
<tr data-subsets="base gct"><td class="enum-pv copyable-cell" title="Stage IIA"><button type="button" class="copy-action pv-copy-icon" data-pv-name="Stage IIA" data-pv-meaning="ncit:C6364" onclick="copyPv(this)" aria-label="Copy permissible value" title="Copy permissible value"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="lucide lucide-copy-icon lucide-copy"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg></button><details class="cell-details"><summary><span>Stage IIA</span></summary></details></td><td class="enum-meaning" title="ncit:C6364"><span><code class="slot-uri">ncit:C6364</code></span></td><td class="enum-description" title="Stage IIA includes: (Any pT/TX, N1, M0, S0); (Any pT/TX, N1, M0, S1).  pTX: Primary tumor cannot be assessed.  N1: Metastasis with a lymph node mass 2 cm or less in greatest dimension; or multiple lymph nodes, none more than 2cm in greatest dimension.  M0: No distant metastasis. S0: Marker study levels within normal limits. S1: LDH less than 1.5 x N (N indicates the upper limit of normal for the LDH assay) and hCG less than 5,000 and AFP less than 1,000.
